title: DNA binding contributes to dominant-negative effects of a catalytically inactive RecQ4-family helicase.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unpacked the full supplement (27.8 MB zip). It holds exactly three items: 'Supplementary File S2.csv' (904 rows x 6 columns of human RECQL4 somatic mutations copied from COSMIC, a cancer mutation catalogue; columns Position, CDS Mutation, AA Mutation, Legacy Mutation ID, Count, Type; 761 unique amino-acid changes, 564 missense, Count median 1, max 163), 'Supplementary File S1.zip' (139 MB unpacked: AlphaFold3 structure prediction of one protein, S. cerevisiae Hrq1 with two zinc ions, 5 model .cif files plus 84 MB of multiple-sequence-alignment files), and 'Supplementary materials.docx', whose text I extracted: Table S1 = 24 yeast strains, Table S2 = 7 plasmids, Table S3 = 28 Hrq1 mutations with ESM-1v, FoldX and MAESTRO computed scores. No measured phenotype table anywhere.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The suppressor-screen counts (43 suppressors screened by amplicon sequencing, 36 carrying a second-site HRQ1 mutation; ~28 whole genomes sequenced across four strain backgrounds; 24 missense suppressor mutations analysed in silico) come from the Results text and Tables 1 and 2 in the article body, not from any downloadable file. The growth phenotypes themselves are serial-dilution spot-assay photographs in Figs 1-6; I did not find any numeric growth data. No sequencing accession appears anywhere in the text and the data availability statement ends with 'shared upon reasonable request'.

a1_downloadable.note: The supplement itself downloads freely and I opened every file. But the only measured data of any scale, the whole-genome sequencing of ~28 suppressor clones, has no accession and the statement says it 'will be shared upon reasonable request'.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The outcome of interest, sensitivity to the crosslinking agent diepoxybutane, exists only as photographs of ten-fold dilution spots in the figures. It would have to be constructed by eye-scoring images; there is no phenotype column in any file.

a3_inputs_present.note: The Hrq1 protein sequence and an AlphaFold3 structure are present, and amino-acid changes are written out (e.g. A1006P), so inputs would not need lookups.

a4_units_stated.note: FAIL for the phenotype: spot assays are reported as qualitative '+' to '++++' relative sensitivity with no units. Table S3's FoldX/MAESTRO values do carry kcal/mol-style units but those are predictions, not measurements.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, badly. 36 suppressor clones with second-site mutations, 24 unique missense changes scored in Table S3. The 904-row COSMIC CSV is a mutation catalogue with no functional outcome attached. The checklist floor is ~400 rows for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~28 MB compressed supplement; 139 MB unpacked if the AlphaFold archive is kept
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized; the only large files are multiple-sequence alignments that would be discarded.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The CSV's 904 rows and Table S3's 28 mutations are consistent with how the paper describes them; no conflicting counts found.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL. The only numeric table in the whole supplement (Table S3) is entirely output from three predictors: ESM-1v, a protein language model; FoldX, a force-field stability calculator; and MAESTRO, a stability predictor. Training on those would distil other models, and the paper itself notes they get C979 wrong.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) would be the natural backbone for variant effects on a helicase
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for ~36 sequences, but there is nothing to fit a head to
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; irrelevant here because no labelled set exists

integration.partner_dataset: COSMIC (cancer somatic mutation catalogue) is already partly copied into the supplement, and human RECQL4 variants could in principle be joined to ClinVar or AlphaFold DB
integration.join_key: UniProt accession plus residue position (Hrq1 is Q05549; human RECQL4 is O94761)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could not write one that this paper's data answers: it contributes 36 yeast suppressor clones with image-based phenotypes, which adds no labelled rows to any variant-effect resource.

controls.positive_control: The K318A catalytic-dead allele itself (ESM-1v score -14.9, the most deleterious in Table S3) would be the obvious control, but with 24 scored mutations there is nothing to control.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless at n=24-36.
controls.external_validation: None: no second yeast suppressor screen of this allele exists, and the COSMIC list carries no functional readout.

honest_claim_h3: Any model built here could only claim 'predicts, from 24 hand-picked missense changes in one yeast protein, whether a mutation was recovered as a suppressor in one lab's screen' - a claim too narrow and too underpowered to be worth making.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence and structure to predict which second mutations switch off a broken DNA-repair helicase's harmful effect.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would show a model each mutated position in the yeast helicase Hrq1, as sequence context plus predicted structure. I verified the available examples number 36 suppressor clones, covering 24 unique missense changes.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a given second-site mutation rescues growth on diepoxybutane, a DNA-crosslinking poison. The true answer comes from photographs of ten-fold dilution spot assays on agar plates, read by eye; there is no numeric growth measurement in the files.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups studying human RECQL4 and Rothmund-Thomson syndrome would like to know which partial loss-of-function variants are actively harmful rather than merely inactive; but 24 labelled mutations cannot answer that, so nothing would be learned here.

ml_idea: The only machine-learning-shaped idea is predicting suppressor status for mutations in the helicase Hrq1 from sequence and predicted structure. With 24 unique missense labels read off plate photographs, and the supplement's only numeric columns being ESM-1v, FoldX and MAESTRO predictions, this is a figure-legend-scale analysis, not a model. The paper is a well-done mechanistic study whose outputs are images, strain tables and three computed score columns.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from file sizes I measured: a 28 MB supplement, 139 MB unpacked, and at most a few dozen sequences to embed. Nothing timed because there is no modelling task to time.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the labelled rows: open 'Supplementary materials.docx' and read Table S3 - 28 mutations, of which 24 missense. That kills it in five minutes, which is what happened.

verdict_reason: Mechanistic yeast-genetics paper. Only 36 suppressor clones / 24 unique missense mutations (A5), the phenotype exists only as spot-assay photographs with qualitative '+' scores rather than a column with units (A2, A4), and the supplement's one numeric table is entirely ESM-1v, FoldX and MAESTRO predictions, so any label would be another model's output (A8). The whole-genome sequencing is not deposited anywhere, only 'available on request'.
